description: From-scratch in-file sBPF disassembler in a new `disasm` namespace, wired into the ELF path via -d/--disassemble/--disassemble-all/--disassemble=<sym> (design §6-§7). Verbatim murmur3_32, comptime syscall hash table, Decoder.decodeOne, Annotator (resolve + region), driver run() as the single Annotator construction site. Depends on FEAT-002 (header, section array, symbol value->name table). sBPF-only; other machines emit a clear 'not implemented' error.
steps: Define `const Error = Io.Writer.Error || error{ParseFailure};` and the types from §6.1: `const SymName = struct { value: u64, name: []const u8 };`, `const SyscallHash = struct { hash: u32, name: []const u8 };`, and `const Annotator = struct { syms: []const SymName, syscalls: []const SyscallHash, machine: std.elf.EM, fn resolve(a, imm: u64) ?[]const u8 (match syscall hash on @truncate(imm) then symbol value==imm), fn region(a, addr: u64) ?[]const u8 (switch addr>>32: 0x1 program,0x2 stack,0x3 heap,0x4 input, else null) };`.

Add `fn murmur3_32(key: []const u8) u32` copied VERBATIM from src/codegen/llvm.sig L58: seed 0; c1=0xcc9e2d51, c2=0x1b873593; per-4-byte LE block `k *%= c1; k = std.math.rotl(u32,k,15); k *%= c2; h ^= k; h = std.math.rotl(u32,h,13); h = h *% 5 +% 0xe6546b64;`; 1-3 byte tail mix with c1/rotl(15)/c2; finalize `h ^= key.len; h ^= h>>16; h *%= 0x85ebca6b; h ^= h>>13; h *%= 0xc2b2ae35; h ^= h>>16;`.

Build a comptime `syscalls: []const SyscallHash` by hashing the §7.3 name list with murmur3_32 at comptime: sol_log_, sol_log_64_, sol_log_pubkey, sol_log_compute_units_, sol_sha256, sol_keccak256, sol_blake3, sol_memcpy_, sol_memmove_, sol_memcmp_, sol_memset_, sol_invoke_signed_c, sol_invoke_signed_rust, sol_get_clock_sysvar, sol_get_rent_sysvar, sol_get_epoch_schedule_sysvar, sol_get_fees_sysvar, sol_get_stack_height, sol_create_program_address, sol_try_find_program_address, sol_secp256k1_recover, sol_curve_validate_point, sol_curve_group_op, abort, sol_panic_, sol_alloc_free_, sol_set_return_data, sol_get_return_data.

Implement `fn decodeOne(code: []const u8, pc: u64, ann: *const Annotator, w: *Io.Writer) Error!usize` for sBPF (eBPF 64-bit LE): instruction `opcode: u8, dst: u4, src: u4 (low nibble=dst, high nibble=src of the byte after opcode), off: i16, imm: i32` = 8 bytes. opcode 0x18 (lddw) is a 16-byte pair: imm64 = (hi<<32)|(lo & 0xffffffff). BOUNDS-CHECK code.len>=8 (and >=16 for 0x18) BEFORE slicing; short tail -> emit `<truncated>` + remaining raw bytes and return error.ParseFailure. Decode classes: ALU/ALU64 (add/sub/mul/div/or/and/lsh/rsh/neg/mod/xor/mov/arsh), JMP/JMP32 (ja/jeq/jgt/jge/jlt/jle/jset/jne/jsgt/jsge/jslt/jsle/call/exit), LD/LDX/ST/STX (b/h/w/dw, [dst+off]/[src+off]). Render `<mnemonic> <operands>` with r0..r10, signed off, hex imm. Unknown opcode -> `<unknown opcode 0xNN>` + raw bytes (non-fatal, 8-byte stride). For `call <imm>` annotate via ann.resolve (syscall hash first, then symbol); for load/store/lddw append ann.region when it returns non-null.

Implement `fn run(d: *const DumpContext, header, sections, syms)` as the SINGLE Annotator construction site: build sorted value->name syms from the FEAT-002 symbol table, pair with the comptime syscalls table and header.machine. For each shf.EXECINSTR section (or the --disassemble=<sym> range): `try d.fr.seekTo(shdr.offset); const code = try r.readAlloc(d.gpa, shdr.size); defer d.gpa.free(code);` with an EOF/bounds check that shdr.offset+shdr.size <= file size (else d.failParse("section bytes out of bounds", .{})); print element-gated section/symbol banner (entry banner at e_entry==0x100000000==MM_PROGRAM_START); walk code with a cursor passing code[cursor..] and pc=base+cursor to decodeOne; print `  <pc>:  <raw-bytes>  <mnemonic ops>  <ann>` with addresses through redaction-aware helpers.

Decoder selection (§6.2): EM.BPF -> sBPF path (version from sbpfVersionName/e_flags); EM.X86_64/EM.AARCH64/EM.RISCV/others/wasm -> clear `"disassembly not implemented for {t}"` error (printed or returned error.ParseFailure), never a stub.
Call disasm.run from the elf path when d.opts.disassemble is set, after the inspection views.
acceptance_criteria: murmur3_32 reproduces the reference immediates (sol_log_=0x207559bd, sol_memcpy_=0x717cc4a3, sol_sha256=0x11f49d86, abort=0xb6fc1a11, sol_try_find_program_address=0x48504a38, sol_get_clock_sysvar=0xd56b5fe9, ""==0) — pinned by the FEAT-005 unit test.
decodeOne renders mov/add/ldxdw/call/exit/lddw correctly; a short tail yields <truncated>+ParseFailure (no out-of-bounds read); an unknown opcode renders inline and the walk continues.

`sig objdump -d <sbpf.so>` (when buildable) shows instructions with syscall-name annotations on matching call immediates and memory-region notes on recognizable addresses; a non-sBPF machine prints the clear 'not implemented' message.
verification: & "C:\Just-Things\Projects\Lib\sig-latest\bin\sig.exe" test lib/compiler/objdump.sig  (compiles + runs the murmur3/decode unit tests added in FEAT-005)

Manual (if Solana target available): `sig build-lib -dynamic -target sbf-solana-solana -mcpu sbpfv3 -O ReleaseSmall -fno-compiler-rt -femit-bin=log.so entry.sig` then `sig objdump -d log.so`; else record the unit-test pass + rationale in findings.
findings:
DONE. All edits confined to lib/compiler/objdump.sig (worktree copy; COFF arm and every coff.* fn untouched; no sig-out/.build copy edited). `sig test lib/compiler/objdump.sig` compiles clean under strict mode -> All 0 tests passed (the murmur3/decode unit tests themselves land in FEAT-005; this gate proves the from-scratch decoder + Annotator type-check under strict allocator discipline).

IMPLEMENTED (new `const disasm = struct {...}` namespace, inserted right after the `elf` namespace closes, before `const macho`):
- `const Error = Io.Writer.Error || error{ParseFailure};`.
- `const SymName = elf.SymName;` (alias; the elf namespace builds+sorts the value->name table in FEAT-002, we consume it read-only).
- `const SyscallHash = struct { hash: u32, name: []const u8 };`.
- `const MM_PROGRAM_START: u64 = 0x1_0000_0000;` (entry banner + 'program' region base).
- `const Annotator = struct { syms: []const SymName, syscalls: []const SyscallHash, machine: std.elf.EM, fn resolve(a, imm: u64) ?[]const u8, fn region(a, addr: u64) ?[]const u8 }`. resolve matches @truncate(imm) against the syscall hash table first, then a symbol whose .value==imm. region switches addr>>32: 0x1 program, 0x2 stack, 0x3 heap, 0x4 input, else null.
- `fn murmur3_32(key: []const u8) u32` copied VERBATIM from src/codegen/llvm.sig L58 (seed 0; c1=0xcc9e2d51, c2=0x1b873593; LE block read, rotl15/rotl13, h=h*%5+%0xe6546b64; tail mix; finalize ^=len, >>16 *%0x85ebca6b >>13 *%0xc2b2ae35 >>16).
- Comptime `const syscalls: []const SyscallHash` built by hashing the §7.3 name list (`const syscall_names = [_][]const u8{ ... }`, 28 names: sol_log_, sol_log_64_, sol_log_pubkey, sol_log_compute_units_, sol_sha256, sol_keccak256, sol_blake3, sol_memcpy_, sol_memmove_, sol_memcmp_, sol_memset_, sol_invoke_signed_c, sol_invoke_signed_rust, sol_get_clock_sysvar, sol_get_rent_sysvar, sol_get_epoch_schedule_sysvar, sol_get_fees_sysvar, sol_get_stack_height, sol_create_program_address, sol_try_find_program_address, sol_secp256k1_recover, sol_curve_validate_point, sol_curve_group_op, abort, sol_panic_, sol_alloc_free_, sol_set_return_data, sol_get_return_data) at comptime via a `blk:` block that copies the array out to a const before taking its address.
- `fn decodeOne(code: []const u8, pc: u64, ann: *const Annotator, w: *Io.Writer) Error!usize`. 8-byte base layout via `const Insn = struct { opcode:u8, dst:u4, src:u4, off:i16, imm:i32 }` + `fn readInsn(code)` (dst=low nibble of byte1, src=high nibble, off/imm little-endian). Bounds-checked `code.len>=8` (and `>=16` for opcode 0x18 lddw) BEFORE any slice; short tail emits `<truncated> <hex bytes>` and returns error.ParseFailure. Classes by opcode&0x07: ALU=0x04 (suffix "32")/ALU64=0x07 via aluOp (add/sub/mul/div/or/and/lsh/rsh/neg/mod/xor/mov/arsh; neg takes no source; imm vs src by bit3); JMP=0x05/JMP32=0x06 via jmpOp (ja/jeq/jgt/jge/jlt/jle/jset/jne/jsgt/jsge/jslt/jsle/call/exit; call annotates via ann.resolve(@truncate imm); exit/ja special-cased); LD/LDX/ST/STX=0x00..0x03 with memSize w/h/b/dw (ldx/st/stx operand forms with signed off printed as +/-0xN; lddw 0x18 reads the 16-byte pair imm64=(hi<<32)|(lo&0xffffffff) and appends ann.region when non-null; ldx appends ann.region on the offset). Unknown opcode -> `<unknown opcode 0xNN> <hex>` and returns 8 (non-fatal, walk continues). Return value is the byte STRIDE (8, or 16 for lddw).
- `fn run(d, hdr: *const std.elf.Header, sections: *const std.ArrayList(std.elf.Elf64.Shdr), shstrtab: []const u8, syms: []const SymName, e_flags: u32) !void` -- the SINGLE Annotator construction site. Decoder selection first: hdr.machine .BPF/.SBF -> sBPF path; anything else -> d.failParse("disassembly not implemented for {s}", .{machineName(m)}) (machineName uses std.enums.tagName, never `{t}` which panics on unnamed non-exhaustive values per the FEAT-002 toolchain finding). Builds the one Annotator{syms, syscalls, machine}. For each section with flags.shf.EXECINSTR (and size!=0, honoring --only-section via filterMatches and the --disassemble=<sym> range filter): EOF/bounds guard `shdr.offset>file_size or shdr.offset+shdr.size>file_size -> d.failParse("section '...' bytes out of bounds")`; then `fr.seekTo(shdr.offset); const codebytes = try r.readAlloc(d.gpa, shdr.size); defer d.gpa.free(codebytes);`. Walks with a cursor: pc=shdr.addr+cursor, prints a `<addr> <name>:` banner when a symbol value==pc, an entry marker at pc==MM_PROGRAM_START, then `  <addr>:  ` (addr via coff.fmtIntField(.va) so -s redaction applies) + decodeOne output; on error.ParseFailure (short tail) it finishes the line and breaks that section.
- Wired into the elf path: in elf.dump, after --dynamic, `if (d.opts.disassemble) try disasm.run(d, &hdr, &sections, shstrtab, sym_names.items, e_flags);`.

SYMBOL-TABLE SOURCING CHANGE (so -d can annotate call targets even without --symbols): elf.dumpSymbols gained a trailing `print_rows: bool` param. The SYMTAB pass now runs whenever `d.opts.symbols or d.opts.disassemble`, but prints its header/table-header/rows/trailing-newline ONLY when print_rows is true (= d.opts.symbols). So `-d` alone still populates the retained+sorted sym_names table silently; `--symbols` prints as before; the DYNSYM pass is unchanged (print_rows=true). This keeps COFF untouched and leaves non-disasm ELF output byte-identical to FEAT-002.

API DETAILS FEAT-005 TESTS NEED (all inside `const disasm = struct {...}` in lib/compiler/objdump.sig; none are `pub`, so FEAT-005 test blocks live in the same file and call them unqualified from a `test` block, or qualified as `disasm.*` from elsewhere in-file):
1. murmur3: `disasm.murmur3_32(key: []const u8) u32`. Reference immediates to pin (match src/codegen/llvm.sig L97 vector): sol_log_=0x207559bd, sol_memcpy_=0x717cc4a3, sol_sha256=0x11f49d86, abort=0xb6fc1a11, sol_try_find_program_address=0x48504a38, sol_get_clock_sysvar=0xd56b5fe9, ""==0x00000000.
2. decode: `disasm.decodeOne(code: []const u8, pc: u64, ann: *const disasm.Annotator, w: *Io.Writer) disasm.Error!usize`. It WRITES the rendered text to `w` and RETURNS the byte stride (usize): 8 for normal/unknown, 16 for lddw (opcode 0x18), error.ParseFailure for a short tail. To unit-test render strings, give it a `std.Io.Writer` over a fixed buffer (e.g. std.Io.Writer.fixed(&buf)) and compare the written slice; build a throwaway Annotator with empty slices: `const ann: disasm.Annotator = .{ .syms = &.{}, .syscalls = disasm.syscalls, .machine = .BPF };` (or .syscalls = &.{} if syscall annotation is not under test). Hand-encoded 8-byte LE opcodes for the §-required cases: mov r0, imm = opcode 0xb7 (ALU64 mov, imm); add r1, imm = 0x07; mov r0,r1 (reg) = 0xbf; ldxdw r0,[r1+off] = 0x79 (LDX, size dw); exit = 0x95; lddw r0, imm64 = 0x18 (needs the 16-byte pair, second 8 bytes carry the high imm in bytes[4..8]). Register byte = (src<<4)|dst. call = 0x85 (imm form); call annotation requires a matching syscall hash in ann.syscalls or a symbol whose value==@truncate(imm).
3. types for building test inputs: `disasm.Annotator`, `disasm.SyscallHash`, `disasm.SymName` (= elf.SymName {value:u64,name:[]const u8}), `disasm.Error`, and the comptime `disasm.syscalls: []const SyscallHash` table.
